--- title: "Case study: the 2011 secession of South Sudan" subtitle: "Spillovers along a trade network, measured in percent of GDP" --- ```{=html}
Run this walkthrough yourself: ▶ Open in Colab
``` In July 2011 South Sudan seceded from Sudan, taking three quarters of the oil fields with it. The paper's second application asks what the split cost "the Sudans" (Sudan and South Sudan combined) in GDP per capita — and where the shock traveled. Spillovers here are not geographic: they move along trade links, so the spatial weights are average pre-period bilateral trade volumes rather than shared borders. ::: {.callout-note} ## MCMC budget in this tutorial Tutorial scale again (`m_iter=4000, burn=2000`). The paper's production run for this application used one million iterations — $\rho$ mixes slowly and this panel is short ($T_0 = 11$ pre-treatment years), so treat the numbers on this page as illustrative. ::: ## Load the data ::: {#fd7fd7f2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from scspill.data import load_sudan panel = load_sudan() panel.df.head(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: The outcome is GDP per capita (constant 2015 US$) and six World Development Indicators enter as covariates: ::: {#1e982762 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} panel.outcome, panel.covariates ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ('gdp_pc', ('exports_gdp_share', 'merchandise_trade_gdp_share', 'trade_gdp_share', 'clean_fuels_access', 'inflation', 'net_migration')) ``` ::: ::: The exposure vector is raw bilateral trade with Sudan — Egypt and Kenya dominate (the estimator normalizes it internally): ::: {#79d5ef43 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} panel.spatial_w.sort_values(ascending=False).head(5) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` country Egypt, Arab Rep. 3.311366e+14 Kenya 8.221436e+13 Uganda 5.884262e+13 South Africa 2.952293e+13 Tunisia 1.206114e+13 Name: amount, dtype: float64 ``` ::: ::: ## Fit ::: {#826dad0e .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} from scspill import SCSPILL result = SCSPILL( { **panel.config_kwargs(), "m_iter": 4000, "burn": 2000, "step_rho": 0.02, "seed": 20251022, "display_graphs": False, } ).fit() print(f"ATT: {result.att:.1f} US$ per capita " f"(95% CrI [{result.att_ci[0]:.1f}, {result.att_ci[1]:.1f}])") print(f"rho: {result.rho_hat:.3f} " f"(95% CrI [{result.rho_ci[0]:.3f}, {result.rho_ci[1]:.3f}])") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ATT: -31.4 US$ per capita (95% CrI [-164.8, 97.9]) rho: 0.476 (95% CrI [0.414, 0.549]) ``` ::: ::: ::: {#1d1a3716 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} result.plot(kind="full", display=False); ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` findfont: Failed to find font weight medium, now using 400. findfont: Failed to find font weight medium, now using 400. findfont: Failed to find font weight medium, now using 400. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Observed vs. counterfactual GDP per capita for the Sudans.](sudan_files/figure-html/cell-6-output-2.png){width=716 height=477} ::: ::: ## Effects in percent The paper reports the secession loss as a percentage of the counterfactual: ::: {#e416b0f7 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np T0 = result.inputs.T0 cf_post = result.effects_detail.cf_mean[T0:] gap_post = result.inputs.Y0[T0:] - cf_post years = result.inputs.time_labels[T0:] for year, g, c in zip(years, gap_post, cf_post): print(f"{year}: {g:+7.1f} US$ ({100 * g / c:+5.1f}% of counterfactual)") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` 2011: +352.5 US$ (+26.3% of counterfactual) 2012: -101.7 US$ ( -7.6% of counterfactual) 2013: -137.8 US$ ( -9.9% of counterfactual) 2014: -127.2 US$ ( -9.0% of counterfactual) 2015: -143.1 US$ (-10.3% of counterfactual) ``` ::: ::: ## Spillovers travel the trade network ::: {#1b20d682 .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} result.plot(kind="spill_top", top_n=6, display=False); ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` findfont: Failed to find font weight medium, now using 400. ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Top spillover paths: the shock lands on Sudan's largest trade partners.](sudan_files/figure-html/cell-8-output-2.png){width=1358 height=515} ::: ::: ::: {#12d2e36f .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} spill_post = result.spillover_panel.loc[2011:] spill_post.abs().mean().sort_values(ascending=False).head(5).round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ``` unit Egypt, Arab Rep. 55.97 Kenya 19.52 Uganda 16.31 Algeria 12.00 Tunisia 9.63 dtype: float64 ``` ::: ::: ## Notes on this application - The treated unit "Sudan" aggregates Sudan and South Sudan after 2011, so the estimand is the effect of the split on the combined economy. - With $T_0 = 11$ pre-periods and 33 donors, the horseshoe prior is doing real work: it shrinks most donor weights to zero and concentrates the fit on a few economies. - $\rho$ is estimated around 0.4 here versus about 0.2 in the California application — trade integration transmits more of the shock than a single land border.
